nodes.text: And Empedocles of Acragas was called Wind-Stopper. It is said, then, that once, when a wind was blowing from the mountain of Acragas, heavy and unhealthy for the inhabitants, and also causing barrenness in their wives, he stopped the wind; and so he himself writes in his verses: 'You will stop the might of the tireless winds, which, rushing upon the earth, waste the fields of mortals; and again, when you wish, you will bring the winds back in return.' And he said that there followed him some who were in need of prophecies, and others long pierced by grievous diseases. Clearly, then, they have come to believe from our Scriptures that the righteous perform healings and signs and wonders; for even if certain powers move the winds and distribute the rains, still let them hear the Psalmist: 'How beloved are your dwellings, Lord of the powers.' He is the Lord of the powers and of the principalities and of the authorities, of whom Moses says, so that we may be with him: 'And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and you shall no longer stiffen your neck; for the Lord your God, he is Lord of lords and God of gods, the great and mighty God', and what follows. And Isaiah says: 'Lift up your eyes on high and see: who has shown forth all these things?'

There are, then, forty-two books of Hermes that are absolutely essential; of these, the thirty-six that contain the whole philosophy of the Egyptians are learned by heart by those already mentioned, and the remaining six by the *pastophoroi* [shrine-bearers], these being medical: on the structure of the body, on diseases, on instruments, on drugs, on eye diseases, and lastly on women's disorders.

And these same people, who bow down, as the saying goes, to every stick and every oiled stone, are afraid of red wool, grains of salt, torches, squill and sulphur, bewitched by sorcerers in certain impure purifications. But God, the one who is truly God, knows only the character of the just man as holy, just as [he knows] the unjust and wicked as accursed. One can see, at any rate, that the eggs [taken] from those who have been purified, if they are kept warm, hatch into living things. But this would not happen if they took up the evils of the one who was purified.
